Amortized Image Reconstruction (AIR) is a self-supervised feed-forward framework that reconstructs a target image into a set of 2D Gaussian primitives in a single network pass, eliminating the costly per-image iterative optimization required by prior methods like GaussianImage [S1, unofficial].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence. The evidence explicitly states that AIR is a 'self-supervised feed-forward framework' (Source [S1] Abstract, Introduction). It confirms that AIR 'amortizes iterative Gaussian fitting into a single network pass' and 'eliminating per-image test-time optimization' (Source [S1] Abstract, Notes). It also details that the method reconstructs an image into '2D Gaussian primitives' (Source [S1] Notes, Method section) and contrasts this with GaussianImage, which 'optimizes Gaussian primitives independently for each image with costly per-image fitting' (Source [S1] Notes). All specific facts in the claim are present in the provided text.

*   **Memory Complexity:** Uses an image-adaptive quantizer for compact Gaussian storage, reducing memory footprint compared to unquantized representations [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the abstract and Section III that the AIR framework is 'equipped with an image-adaptive quantizer for compact Gaussian storage.' This directly supports the claim's assertion regarding the use of an image-adaptive quantizer for compact storage. Furthermore, the claim states this reduces the memory footprint compared to unquantized representations; since quantization is inherently a technique to reduce data size (and thus memory footprint) compared to full precision (unquantized) representations, and the text highlights 'compact Gaussian storage' as a feature, the claim is fully supported by the provided text.

It further clarifies that 'the predictor outputs a stage-specific Gaussian primitive set added to the accumulated representation.' This directly supports the mathematical claim that the accumulated set at stage k is the union of the previous set and the new primitives ($G_k = G_{k-1} U Delta G_k$).

Direct supervision with rendering loss is unstable due to the under-constrained mapping from image space to Gaussian space [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that direct supervision with rendering loss is unstable due to the under-constrained mapping from image space to Gaussian space. where $d_{n,p} = p - \mu_n$ is the offset vector [S1, unofficial].

Mathematically, an offset from a center point ($μ_n$) to a target point (pixel $p$) is calculated as the target coordinate minus the source coordinate, i.e., $p - μ_n$. Therefore, the claim matches the definition provided in the text.
